background.task:
Successfully extracted 20 book titles and prices from `http://books.toscrape.com/` using browser4-cli's X-SQL query engine via all four input methods:

| Method | Command | Result |
|--------|---------|--------|
| Inline `--sql` | `htmlsnapshot query --sql "SELECT ..."` | ✅ 20 rows |
| File `--sql @file` | `htmlsnapshot query --sql @extract_books.sql` | ✅ 20 rows |
| Stdin `--sql-stdin` | `htmlsnapshot query --sql-stdin < extract_books.sql` | ✅ 20 rows |
| Base64 `--sql-base64` | `htmlsnapshot query --sql-base64 <encoded>` | ✅ 20 rows |
| Result-only | `--result-only` | ✅ Clean JSON array |

**X-SQL query used:**
```sql
SELECT
    DOM_FIRST_TEXT(DOM, 'h3') AS title,
    DOM_FIRST_TEXT(DOM, 'p.price_color') AS price
FROM DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT(@url, 'article.product_pod')
WHERE DOM_IS_NOT_NIL(DOM)
```

Selectors discovered via `htmlsnapshot inspect`: container `article.product_pod` (20 matches), title `h3`, price `p.price_color`.

issues.title: htmlsnapshot inspect doesn't surface title attribute as alternative for truncated text

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run `htmlsnapshot inspect` on books.toscrape.com. Inspect output shows `h3` text as "A Light in the ..." (truncated) but doesn't mention that the child `<a title="Full Title">` attribute contains the full text.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Inspect should note when visible text is truncated and suggest checking child element attributes (e.g., `<a title>` or `img alt`) for complete values.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Inspect shows truncated text content from h3 elements without indicating that the full title is available via `DOM_FIRST_ATTR(DOM, 'h3 a', 'title')`.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The inspect tool extracts `textContent` from DOM nodes which reflects CSS `text-overflow: ellipsis` truncation. It doesn't check whether child elements have attributes (like `title`) that contain fuller text. This is a heuristic gap — the tool could compare text length vs attribute length to detect truncation.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- In inspect output, for elements with truncated text (ending in '...'), check child elements for title attributes with fuller text and surface them as alternative selectors
- Add a column or annotation showing that DOM_FIRST_ATTR may yield fuller text than DOM_FIRST_TEXT for certain elements
- Consider adding a PowerCSS pattern or heuristic to detect text-overflow truncation vs genuine ellipsis

issues.title: Relationship between htmlsnapshot capture and htmlsnapshot query is unclear

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Read the help text for `htmlsnapshot` and `htmlsnapshot query`. The former says it stores a snapshot for later querying; the latter says it runs X-SQL 'against the HTML snapshot stored in Browser4's page storage' but `DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT` actually re-fetches the page independently.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Clear documentation explaining that `htmlsnapshot query` with `DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT(@url, ...)` fetches the page fresh (not from the stored snapshot), while `htmlsnapshot inspect` and `htmlsnapshot get` use the stored snapshot from a prior `htmlsnapshot` capture.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The help text for `htmlsnapshot query` says it runs 'against the HTML snapshot stored in Browser4's page storage via the scrape API' which contradicts the behavior of `DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT` which loads the page fresh. A user needs to run `htmlsnapshot` capture for `inspect` but may not need it for `query`.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The `htmlsnapshot query` command description conflates two concepts: the stored snapshot (used by `get`/`inspect`/`summary`) and the scrape API (used by `DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT` which re-fetches). The help text wasn't updated when the X-SQL scrape API was added.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/ — help text definition for the htmlsnapshot query subcommand

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Clarify in the help text that `htmlsnapshot query` with `DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT` re-fetches the page via the scrape API, independent of the stored snapshot
- Add a note that `htmlsnapshot` capture is only needed for `inspect`/`get`/`summary`, not for `query` with `@url`
- Consider renaming or restructuring: `query` belongs more naturally under its own namespace since it doesn't actually use the stored snapshot

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Compare `htmlsnapshot query --help` examples (lowercase `dom_first_text`, `load_and_select`) with `references/x-sql.md` and `references/x-sql-dom-load-select.md` (uppercase `DOM_FIRST_TEXT`, `DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT`).

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The --help text examples were likely written independently from the reference docs without a style guide for function name casing. The H2 SQL engine is case-insensitive so both work.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ or wherever help text strings are defined for the htmlsnapshot query command

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Standardize on one casing convention (prefer UPPERCASE to match the reference docs)
- Update --help examples to match the reference documentation casing
- Add a note in the reference docs that function names are case-insensitive

issues.title: Cargo dev-profile warning pollutes stderr output on every invocation

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run any `./b4w.ps1` command. Observe the line `warning: browser4-cli@4.12.0: browser4-cli: embedded 31 skill files from /home/vincent/workspace/Browser4-4.12/skills` printed to stderr before every command.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Clean output without build-system warnings in normal operation. Warnings should only appear during actual compilation.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Every invocation prints a cargo warning to stderr about embedded skill files, even when the binary is already compiled.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: This is a cargo/rust build warning emitted during the `cargo run` step in `b4w.ps1`. The warning is about the `build.rs` embedding skill files — it fires on every `cargo run` invocation because cargo checks the build script output even when the binary is up to date.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: b4w.ps1 — the cargo run invocation; cli/browser4-cli/build.rs — the build script emitting the warning

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Suppress the specific warning in build.rs or Cargo.toml if it's expected behavior
- In b4w.ps1, filter stderr to remove known benign warnings before displaying to the user
- Consider using `cargo build` + running the binary directly instead of `cargo run` to avoid re-triggering the warning

issues.title: htmlsnapshot inspect requires separate htmlsnapshot capture step — 4-step workflow for data extraction

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: To discover selectors and extract data: 1) goto URL, 2) htmlsnapshot capture, 3) htmlsnapshot inspect, 4) htmlsnapshot query. This is 4 separate commands for a task that conceptually could be 2 (goto + query-with-inspect).

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A combined workflow or shortcut that captures, inspects, and suggests a query template in fewer steps. For example, `htmlsnapshot query --inspect` that auto-discovers selectors and runs the extraction in one command.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: User must run 4 separate commands with understanding of which steps are prerequisite for which others.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The `htmlsnapshot` capture and `inspect` are separate architectural layers — capture stores the DOM, inspect reads from storage. There's no combined command that chains them together for the common 'discover selectors and extract' workflow.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add an `htmlsnapshot query --auto` or `--inspect` flag that auto-captures, auto-discovers selectors, and generates a query template
- Document the minimal workflow more prominently: note that `htmlsnapshot query` with `DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT(@url, ...)` works without a prior `htmlsnapshot` capture
- Consider a `quick-extract` meta-command that combines goto + inspect + query
